chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, that Amir al-Mu'minin, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, used to say:

Blessedness is for the one who makes worship and du'a sincerely for Allah, and does not occupy his heart with what his eyes see, and does not forget the dhikr of Allah because of what his ears hear, and does not grieve his breast over what has been given to others.

key_terms.أَخْلَصَ: made pure and sincere solely for Allah
key_terms.أُعْطِيَ غَيْرُهُ: what was given to someone else
key_terms.صَدْرَهُ: his breast or chest, meaning his inner state
key_terms.قَلْبَهُ: his heart, the inner center of awareness and intention

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about sincerity in worship and protecting the heart from worldly distractions?
ai.summary: This hadith praises sincerity in worship and du'a, together with inner discipline over the heart, sight, and hearing. It teaches that true devotion to Allah is joined with dhikr, freedom from distraction, and freedom from sorrow over what others have been given.
